what: A devnet test: which pallets can a FlopSessionKeys session never call, even when its allow list names them?
answer: Seven, as the swarm's reading of the runtime code said: Utility, Proxy, Multisig, Sudo, Scheduler, EmergencyOverride and FlopSessionKeys itself. A session whose allow list named all seven was refused each of them with FlopSessionKeys.PalletNotAllowed. In the same session System.remark, also on the allow list, went through. An allow list entry written in lower case (computechannel) let a ComputeChannel call through to the pallet.
not_shown: That these seven are the whole list (a pallet we did not try could be denied too). That Balances is not denied (not tried; the swarm report says it is not). What an empty allow list permits. Anything about the hosted gateway.
harmless_by_construction: Each call tried was chosen so that it would change nothing even if the chain had let it through: an empty batch, removing proxies the owner does not have, cancelling a multisig operation that does not exist, three calls only root or the sudo key may make, and revoking a session that was already revoked. The signer refuses any other call of these pallets, and never signs EmergencyOverride.execute_override.

device.role: a new key made for this test; the session's delegate

how: Each call was built and signed offline by flop-sign.mjs (version 3, in this folder) on the operator's computer. Before any key was used, check.mjs compared every new call with the polkadot-api reference encoder on the metadata we recorded ourselves: byte for byte the same, and every refusal seen. Each extrinsic was checked by the node with TaggedTransactionQueue_validate_transaction, sent with author_submitAndWatchExtrinsic, and read back from System.Events at the block that finalized it. Events were decoded with the reference decoder and the same metadata.
